problem: The headline "Strongest level reached: pathogenic moderate" is carried mostly by nonsense and canonical-splice variants, where a computational criterion is not the relevant evidence. evidence: Reviewer recomputation from data/genomics/evo2-scores.csv joined to data/genomics/raw/brca1-findlay2018-snvs.csv: at s >= 0.009486 there are 37 LOF, 3 FUNC and 1 INT (41, matching the JSON). Of the 37 LOF, 17 are canonical splice, 8 nonsense, 9 missense, 3 splice region; all 3 FUNC are missense. Missense only: 9 of 57 LOF and 3 of 147 FUNC exceed the threshold. Missense AUROC in the JSON is 0.683 (0.593 to 0.768). README lines 48-61 and line 217.
fix: In genomics/analyse.py compute the likelihood-ratio table and strength for missense variants alone and report "not established" if the bins are too small. Print the consequence mix of the variants above each threshold. Change the headline sentence to say the moderate level is reached on the all-consequence mix and is not shown for missense. problem: The comparison table sets Evo 2 on 423 variants beside CADD and phyloP on all 3,893, and the ClinVar cross-check shows Evo 2's 0.930 with no baseline and no breakdown. The README says the rows cover different sets, but the like-for-like numbers are missing and they change the reading.

problem: The simulator does not reproduce the cohort statistic that the document uses to justify its spread parameter, and the value 0.96 is not derived anywhere. The document computes 0.99 from the whole pathway's mean and median, then assigns 0.96 to each single step. Because the steps are independent, the summed intervals come out much less spread than the cohort, so the per-interval sample sizes may be too small. The 0.6 split that places DIAGNOSIS is also an unsourced constant that sets the diagnostic and treatment columns, and it is not listed among the assumptions.
evidence: Lines 62-64 and 94-96. Reviewer simulation of the same step model (2,000,000 draws, public-route means 72, 22, 53, 57, 3, log-SD 0.96 per step): symptom-to-treatment mean 206.9 days, median 174.1, log-SD 0.548. The cited cohort has mean 207 and median 127 (data/evidence/literature-v1.json), which gives 0.99. With s = 0.9885 the formula gives 1,918 / 524 / 253 / 106 instead of 1,809 / 495 / 239 / 100 (my calculation). src/recommend.mjs line 166 says 0.96 is implied by the paper's mean/median ratio, which contradicts the 0.99 computed here. eventlog/simulate.py line 29: DIAGNOSIS_FRACTION = .6.
fix: Say in section 2 that the simulator matches the published means but not the published median (174 against 127 days on the public route) and that real intervals may be more spread. Either calibrate so the total matches (correlated steps or a larger step SD) or add a sensitivity column. State where 0.96 comes from or call it a choice. Add the 0.6 split and the uniform MDT placement to the listed assumptions. Correct the comment in src/recommend.mjs.

problem: The single pathway order is written as a property of every episode ("Within an episode every event is on or after the one before it"). That is a simulator convention. As a specification for real data it would mark legitimate pathways as violations, for example a first specialist visit before the diagnosis is confirmed, an emergency presentation diagnosed before any referral, or a screening case with no symptom onset.
evidence: Lines 28-39. The order was chosen to match one cohort's milestones (line 36-37) and DIAGNOSIS is placed by a fixed 0.6 fraction in the simulator. The validator counts every reversed pair (line 39).
fix: State that the order is the simulator's convention and that for real data a reversed pair is a flag for review, not an error. List the exceptions to confirm with clinicians before the validator is used on real records.

problem: Repeated quarterly looks are not part of the multiple-comparison family. The early-warning study tests every quarter on a rolling four-quarter window with the single-look Bonferroni threshold (0.05/69), so the 5% family-wise rate holds for one look only. DATA_COLLECTION.md section 2 presents a = 0.05/69 as the multiplicity handling and proposes quarterly reporting.
evidence: design_study.py:302-323 loops q = 0..11 and calls evaluate() with the default critical(comparisons=69) (detect.py:36). Reviewer simulation with the project's own pathways/log_spans/moments/test_moments (23 counties x 250 episodes a quarter, day precision, no slowdown anywhere, each county against the rest of the country, 1000 replications): at least one false flag somewhere in 12 looks in 0.335 of replications (Wilson 0.306 to 0.365); in looks 5 to 12 alone 0.235; mean for a single look 0.042. The stored early_warning rows already show one-county pre-onset false-alarm rates of 0.003 to 0.012 over 4 looks against a single-look nominal of 0.0022. Script and output: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-mikaelervamaa-Library-Application-Support-Claude-scratch-workspaces-5d672b86-628a-4541-8274-071bf0a9e008-6b216046-ec1a-4b9a-9976-dd851f37ac44-scratch-2026-11-14-099cd6/0881be11-baf2-48a2-9868-60cfd5b0055a/scratchpad/review-stats/null_sim_c.py and null_sim_c.json (a first attempt was lost when the process was killed under memory pressure; it was rerun alone).
fix: Count looks in the family: either critical(comparisons=69*L) for a planned horizon of L looks (upper bound), or a sequential boundary (group-sequential or CUSUM) calibrated with this same simulation so that the false-alarm probability over the horizon is 5%. Recompute quarters-to-detection at that boundary, report the family-wise false-alarm rate per horizon next to it, and state in DATA_COLLECTION.md that 0.05/69 covers one look of one stratum (not quarterly repeats, not cancer-site strata).

problem: The headline 'pathogenic: moderate' evidence strength for Evo 2 does not hold for missense variants, the class a computational criterion applies to. It is produced by canonical splice and nonsense variants in the top score bins, and most of the overall AUROC is available from the consequence category alone.
evidence: At the 'moderate' threshold (s >= 0.00949) there are 41 variants: 37 loss-of-function (17 canonical splice, 8 nonsense, 3 splice region, 9 missense), 3 functional (all missense), 1 intermediate. Missense only (57 loss-of-function, 147 functional): 9 against 3 above the threshold, likelihood ratio 6.93 with a one-sided 95% log-Wald lower bound of 2.56 (moderate needs 4.33 or 5.79). Running the module's own analyse() on the 222 scored missense variants gives strongest reached supporting / none with 20 bins (top bin 8 against 3, lower bound 2.55), supporting (Tavtigian) and none (Pejaver) with 10 bins, none with 5 bins. A lookup with no model (loss-of-function rate of the variant's consequence class, cross-fitted by position) reaches AUROC 0.790 on the same 400 labelled variants and 0.758 on the full table, against 0.830 for Evo 2; Evo 2 on missense is 0.683. Scripts: review-stats/gen1.py and gen2.py in the scratchpad named above.
fix: Compute the likelihood-ratio table and the strength reached within missense and make that the headline evidence result; report per-consequence tables for the rest. Add the consequence-only predictor as a baseline row in the comparison table. Reword the summary: on this sample the score reaches at most supporting evidence for missense variants, and the all-variant 'moderate' reflects splice and nonsense variants that other criteria already cover.

problem: The one-sided bootstrap bound on the per-bin likelihood ratio is not valid in sparse bins, and the evidence strength reached changes with the number of bins. The strength thresholds themselves (Tavtigian 2018, Pejaver 2022) are coded correctly; the bound that is compared with them is not.
evidence: local_likelihood_ratios (analyse.py:147-162) resamples the observed classes with fixed edges; a bin with no functional variant can never receive one, so its 'lower bound' is set by the +0.5 constant (analyse.py:141-144). Same data, same code, different --lr-bins: 40 bins gives Tavtigian 'strong' (top bin 10 loss-of-function against 0 functional, reported lower bound 30.7), 20 bins 'moderate', 5 bins Pejaver 'supporting'. Exact conservative bounds (Clopper-Pearson on each class share at 2.5%): 3.75 for the 10-against-0 bin; 6.01 for bin 20 (module 14.58) and 4.32 for bin 19 (module 9.00) of the reported 20-bin table; log-Wald bounds 9.12 and 6.93. Bin 19 therefore sits at or below the moderate target (4.33 Tavtigian, 5.79 Pejaver) under the exact bound.
fix: Replace the percentile bootstrap by an exact or score interval for a ratio of two proportions (Koopman or Miettinen-Nurminen; the Clopper-Pearson pair as a conservative fallback), require a minimum count of each class per bin or use Pejaver's sliding window with a minimum count, fix the bin count before looking at results, and report the 10 / 20 / 40 bin sensitivity in the result file.

problem: The detector's realised false-positive rate exceeds the Bonferroni level for small counties and, much more, when dates are month-precision. The study reports only one family-wise null (23 counties x 250, day precision: 0.058 / 0.043, which I reproduced exactly), so the inflation is not visible in RESULTS.md, and the unit test for the null cannot detect it.
evidence: test_moments (detect.py:33-36) compares a Wald statistic with a county-estimated variance against a normal quantile at z = 3.38. Stored null_by_cell in design-study-v1.json, D3 with half the dates month-precision: 44 false flags in 10 cells x 1000 replications (n = 100 cells: 0.007 and 0.010) against a nominal 0.0022 per county. Reviewer simulation with the project's functions, one county against a 2,000,000-episode reference, any of the three tests: day precision n = 50: 0.0040 (1.8 x nominal), n = 100: 0.0027 (1.2 x), n = 250: 0.0023; month share 0.5 n = 50: 0.0159 (7.3 x), n = 100: 0.0083 (3.8 x), n = 250: 0.0039 (1.8 x), n = 1000: 0.0026 (200,000 / 200,000 / 100,000 / 40,000 replications). Family-wise with month share 0.5: 0.076 (23 x 250), 0.096 (population-proportional counties, 9,250 cases, sizes 50 to 1,136; Wilson 0.086 to 0.107), 0.062 (37,000 cases); the same layouts at day precision give 0.047, 0.045 and 0.049. tests/test_eventlog.py:165-169 accepts any single-county null rate below 0.08. Outputs: review-stats/null_sim.log and null_sim_d.json in the scratchpad named above.
fix: Use Welch t quantiles (or a permutation null) instead of NORM.inv_cdf for the county test; do not run this Wald test on intervals with a month-precision endpoint (test day-precision pairs only, or fit an interval-censored model); set a minimum number of complete day-precision episodes for testing. Extend familywise_null to month share 0.5 and to population-proportional county sizes and report those rates next to 0.058. Tighten test_empirical_null to a bound near the nominal rate with enough replications to resolve it.

problem: The bootstrap intervals treat variants as independent although the sample was drawn by position and the two or three variants at a position share one reference window and usually one class. The reported interval for the headline AUROC is too narrow. The limits text says so in words, but the narrow interval is the one reported.
evidence: stratified_bootstrap (analyse.py:78-85) resamples single variants. The 423 variants sit on 144 positions (136 with three variants); within-position score correlation is 0.71 and in 102 of 143 multi-variant positions all variants have the same class. Resampling positions instead (4,000 resamples) gives 0.752 to 0.897 for the AUROC against the reported 0.781 to 0.879 (46% wider), and 0.570 to 0.787 for missense against 0.593 to 0.768. The point estimate reproduces exactly (0.8298950766747377, also by brute force).
fix: Resample positions (all variants of a drawn position together) in stratified_bootstrap, with_interval and the likelihood-ratio bounds, and regenerate the result file and README.

problem: The risk-coverage figures ('24.0% of notes at <=1% error', '34.0% at <=5%', and 43.5% / 47.8% for the Haiku notes) are chosen and evaluated on the same notes, and the samples are too small to support a 1% limit. RESULTS.md words them as the share of notes that can skip review.
evidence: risk_coverage (metrics.py:91-119) takes the largest coverage whose in-sample risk is under the limit. All stored metrics recompute exactly from the predictions in eval-v1.json. Test set: 48 of 200 admitted with 0 errors, Wilson upper bound 7.4% (exact one-sided 6.1%); Haiku notes: 20 of 46 with 0 errors, upper bound 16.1%. Out of sample the thresholds do not hold: the Haiku '<=1%' threshold (-0.002291) applied to the 200 test notes admits 80 with 6 errors (7.5%, Wilson 3.5% to 15.4%); the test threshold (-0.000438) applied to the Haiku notes admits 11 of 46. None of the 110 test notes with a relative date is admitted, so the score is mostly separating notes with and without relative dates.
fix: Fix the threshold on the 250 validation notes (not used for gradient steps), then report coverage and error on the test notes at that threshold with an exact one-sided upper bound; evaluate all 500 test notes. State that a <=1% claim at 95% confidence needs at least 299 admitted notes without an error, and replace the 'can skip review' wording by the observed count and its upper bound.

problem: The sample-size table uses a one-sample formula (reference treated as infinite), while the detector compares each county with the rest of the country in the same period. The statement that the table is 'accurate to about one percentage point of power' (DATA_COLLECTION.md:112) was checked only against a 50,000,000-episode reference.
evidence: sample_size (power.py:17-19) has no reference term; sample_size_check uses the calibration sample as reference (design_study.py:114, 126). With the project's analytic_power and a comparator of 37,000 - n episodes, power at the tabulated n for a 10% slowdown is 0.771 (primary care, n = 1,728), 0.768 (diagnostic, n = 1,874) and 0.779 (treatment, n = 1,267) instead of 0.80; the n that restores 0.80 is 1,817, 1,980 and 1,314 (+5.2%, +5.7%, +3.7%). For the 20% row against one quarter (9,250 cases) power is 0.766 to 0.778.
fix: Use the two-sample form n(N - n)/N >= s^2 (z + z_power)^2 / (ln r)^2 with N the national count of the period, or keep the table for an infinite reference and print the correction beside it; add a sample-size check cell with a rest-of-country comparator.

problem: Cross-fitting keeps folds apart by variant but not by position: variants that share a position and a reference window are split between the training and the held-out fold.
evidence: stratified_folds (analyse.py:235-242) assigns folds per variant within class. Of 138 positions with more than one labelled variant, 130 have variants in different folds. The effect on the two-parameter calibration is small: Brier 0.1233 as reported, 0.1251 with folds assigned by position, 0.1228 fitted in sample.
fix: Assign folds by position (grouped, stratified on the position's majority class) and report that Brier score.
